title: Of the atlas’s 17 issue records on news, records and public information, two are documented, eight well supported, six plausible and one a hypothesis.
measure_line: Issue records in the atlas’s domain of news, records and public information, each a problem it records with its grade and the month the atlas observed it, as of October 15, 2026, United States.
notes: Grades: Documented, on the public record; Well supported, strong research evidence; Plausible, some evidence; Hypothesis, not yet tested.
The atlas keeps 194 issue records across its ten domains; this lookup holds one domain’s 17.
The still image shows one filter on: the eight records graded well supported.

notes_internal: Data plan row 37 drew the whole register (194 records, atlas-wide). As live text the 194 rows weigh about 25 KB at the least (51 KB with ID, domain and month), over three times the extended average; R6 and DR-238 keep tables live, so the lookup holds one domain's 17 records (4 to 5 KB) and note 2 gives the whole count. The data lead confirmed D01 (A10).
D01 has the most room in chapter 14's count (3 of 95, data lead DL-ED1) and all four grades, so the grade filter has something to do.
The live lookup (search field, grade filter, count line) waits on request A9; until then the figure shows the still and the folded table, both complete.
Every record's ID is listed in v7.ids, so the table prints each in its chip ('Issue I001').
Data lead DL-A6: the title gives each grade its own count. DL-R5: S38 prints the sidecar's domain_d01 variant, which names the one domain drawn.
source_line: Source: Oath & Action’s systems atlas, Who Do They Answer To?, issue records in the domain of news, records and public information, 17 of 194 issues, as of October 15, 2026, United States. Snapshot of October 15, 2026. Grades are the atlas’s own.
